text: Last lesson for Project 1: deploying to a real network, verifying the contract, and writing the README that actually closes this project out.

Before deploying anywhere but your local node: all tests green, a dedicated testnet-only wallet funded from a Sepolia faucet — never a wallet that's ever held real funds — and your constructor arguments ready.
Hardhat 3 configures networks directly in the config file, but pulls secrets through configVariable from an encrypted keystore, not a plain .env file that's easy to accidentally commit.

The Ignition module declares what to deploy and in what order — both tokens first, then the pool, which needs their addresses. Ignition tracks the deployment so a failed run can resume instead of starting over.
Set your secrets in the encrypted keystore, deploy the Ignition module to Sepolia, then verify — publishing your source code so the block explorer matches it to the deployed bytecode.

The finished README is what an interviewer reads before your code: what it is, the architecture, what's deliberately simplified and why, your test coverage, the security checklist with your findings, and the verified, linkable contract addresses.
Project 1 is complete. Project 2 — an NFT marketplace — picks up next, reusing this same arc: kickoff, contract design, frontend, testing, and deployment.
